label: GO win-stay-on-a2 when belief favours S2, scaled by late episode time
explanation: Transcoder candidate feature hidden/197 is active only at GO, mid-to-late in the episode (trials ~50-90; timing baseline peaks in deciles 7-8, drops in decile 9). Beyond timing, its magnitude is a win-stay-on-a2 signal gated by the observed belief that S2 is good: large (~0.6-0.8) at GO after a rewarded a2 trial (mainly a2 S2 r) when the ideal-observer P(S1 good) is low (below ~0.3), scaling with how sure the belief is and how late in the episode (strongest trials 60-89). Window-first trials with no visible previous trial behave the same given belief. Below the timing baseline at GO after any a1 trial, and after unrewarded a2 trials even when belief favours S2. D1 and D2 always zero. Terms: GO x (prev a2 rewarded or unknown) x episode-decile shape x clip(1-3*belief) (dominant); GO x last a2 S2 r x decile shape; GO x prev a2 unrewarded x belief<0.2 x decile shape (negative); GO x prev a1 x decile shape (negative). A five-term version (with an extra belief<0.2 indicator, fitted weight ~0) scored test R^2 beyond timing 0.667 (dev 0.681), above the profile's additive all ceiling 0.38 (all observed 0.31), because the effect is a multiplicative interaction of last outcome, belief and episode time. Observed quantities only (no model value/policy, no future variables); relative to the earlier value/policy explanation, observed belief plus last trial loses little. Timing alone R^2 0.24.

issues: Reproduced the recorded test R^2 beyond timing of 0.667 (timing alone 0.24). The core claim holds. If the belief factor is dropped, a GO x (a2 S2 r or unknown previous trial) x decile-shape term falls to 0.454 test. Keeping the episode window (ep_dec>=4) but dropping the decile shape gives 0.427.

The four terms are needlessly complicated and leave a systematic over-prediction. In misses, GO after a2 S2 u is over-predicted by -0.056 and GO after a2 S1 r by -0.043. The negative 'unrewarded a2' term only covers belief<0.2, so after a2 u trials with belief>=0.2 the model still predicts the positive timing baseline while the feature is about 0. The explanation's sentence 'below baseline after unrewarded a2 even when belief favours S2' is true of the data, but the terms only partly implement it.

A simpler two-term model does better on test. Term 1 is GO x (previous trial a2 rewarded or unknown) x decile shape x clip(1-3*belief). Term 2 is GO x decile shape (negative weight), which lowers every other GO step. This scores 0.689 test (0.694 with a2 S1 r as its own term, weight 1.09 vs 1.63 for a2 S2 r, so rare-rewarded a2 also raises it but less). Its misses leave no systematic class above about 0.008.

The belief threshold is overstated. 'Below about 0.3' is too tight. A wider gate, clip(1-2*belief) (graded up to belief 0.5), scores 0.709 test, against 0.669 for clip(1-4*belief) and 0.668 for a hard belief<0.3 cut. The dependence is graded over the whole S2-favouring half.
The future variable adds nothing. Adding the upcoming choice (action==2) interaction gives 0.691 vs 0.689. The observed-only claim is fine.

The 'late episode' factor is the timing baseline's own decile shape copied in as a multiplier. That is fine as an interaction, but it is not an independent finding about episode time beyond what the baseline already shows.
skeptic.revised_label: GO win-stay-on-a2: after a rewarded a2 trial (or unknown previous trial), scaled by observed belief favouring S2 (graded over belief<0.5) and by the mid/late-episode timing shape; off otherwise at GO
